newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea intervenes to cap dlr rise-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea intervenes to cap dlr rise-dealers.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea (BOK) intervened in the interbank market in early Wednesday morning trading to slow the won's plunge against the dollar, dealers said.
The central bank denied that it had intervened.
Dealers could not confirm the level that the central bank stepped into the market at, but said it was around the 822-823 level.
"Government procurements yesterday increased the demand for dollars. It continued to rise as banks bought dollars to cover short positions," said a foreign bank dealer.
There was a government procurement deal worth about $56 million seen on Tuesday.
After the suspected intervention, the won was trading at 821.20, up from its opening low of 823.50.
